# Penfield

> Penfield is persistent memory for AI assistants. It stores what an AI learns as memories, links them into a knowledge graph, and finds them again with hybrid search, across conversations and across AI apps. An AI connects to Penfield as a remote MCP server at https://mcp.penfield.app, or through the REST API at https://api.penfield.app/api/v2. This file explains Penfield to LLMs and agents and indexes the documentation at https://docs.penfield.app.

Every documentation page is also available as plain Markdown. Take the page path and read it from the public source repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/penfieldlabs/docs/main/{path}.md (for example https://raw.githubusercontent.com/penfieldlabs/docs/main/api/endpoints/memories.md).

## What Penfield stores

- **Memories**: single pieces of knowledge, up to 10,000 characters each. Each has a type (11 types: fact, insight, conversation, correction, reference, task, checkpoint, identity_core, personality_trait, relationship, strategy), an importance and a confidence from 0 to 1, and up to 10 tags.
- **Relationships**: typed, directed links between two memories. There are 24 types in 8 categories, such as supports, contradicts, supersedes, updates, causes, part_of, references and follows. Together they form a knowledge graph that search can follow.
- **Documents**: files the user uploads (text, Markdown, PDF, EPUB, HTML, JSON, YAML, code; up to 20 MB). Penfield splits them into chunks and the chunks are searchable alongside memories.
- **Artifacts**: file storage with a folder tree, up to 1 MB per file. An artifact is saved, read, listed and deleted by its path. Artifacts are not searched. To make one findable, store a memory that describes the file and gives its path.
- **Contexts**: named checkpoints of a work session. One agent saves a context and a later session, or another agent, restores it.
- **Personality**: a persona and custom instructions chosen by the user in the Penfield portal. An AI loads them at the start of a conversation with the awaken call.

Search is hybrid: BM25 keyword search, vector similarity and graph expansion, fused into one ranking. Default weights are 0.4, 0.4 and 0.2.

## How to connect

Choose by what the AI or agent can do.

1. **Remote MCP server.** Preferred for chat apps and agents with MCP support.
   - Server URL: `https://mcp.penfield.app` (root path, no `/mcp` or `/sse`)
   - Transport: streamable HTTP
   - Authentication: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. The client registers itself (dynamic client registration) and the user signs in to Penfield in a browser. API keys are not accepted by the MCP server.
   - Apps call this a connector, custom connector, plugin, app or MCP server.
2. **mcp-remote bridge.** For apps that only start local MCP servers or cannot do the OAuth sign-in: `npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.penfield.app/`
3. **REST API.** For scripts, backends and agents without MCP.
   - Base URL: `https://api.penfield.app/api/v2`
   - API key exchange: `POST /api/v2/auth/token` with `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` returns an access token (24 hours) and a refresh token. All other calls take `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`.
   - OAuth device code flow (RFC 8628) for command-line and headless tools, and authorization code with PKCE for apps with a browser. Endpoints are discovered at `https://api.penfield.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.
   - Scopes: `read`, `write`, `delete`, `profile`, `offline_access`. Deleting needs `delete`.

Users create accounts and API keys, upload documents and set the personality at https://portal.penfield.app.

## MCP tools

The MCP server offers 17 tools.

- `awaken`: load the user's persona and custom instructions. Call it first in every new conversation.
- `store`: save a memory. The memory type is detected from the content.
- `recall`: hybrid search over memories and documents, with tag, date and source filters.
- `search`: the same search as `recall`, in the citation format that ChatGPT connectors require.
- `fetch`: get one memory by id, in citation format.
- `update_memory`: change the content, importance or tags of a memory.
- `connect`: create a relationship between two memories.
- `disconnect`: remove a relationship between two memories.
- `explore`: traverse the knowledge graph from a memory.
- `save_context`: save a named checkpoint with a narrative description.
- `restore_context`: load a checkpoint by name.
- `list_contexts`: list saved checkpoints.
- `reflect`: analyze recent memories for topics and patterns.
- `save_artifact`: save a file at a path.
- `retrieve_artifact`: read a file by path.
- `list_artifacts`: list one folder.
- `delete_artifact`: delete a file by path.

There is no MCP tool that deletes a memory. Memories are deleted through the REST API or the portal.

## Guidance for an AI that uses Penfield

- Call `awaken` at the start of each conversation and follow the briefing it returns.
- Call `recall` before answering anything that may depend on earlier conversations.
- Call `store` when something is worth keeping: a decision, a fact about the user or their work, a correction, an insight. Write complete, self-contained thoughts. Add tags (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, up to 50 characters).
- After storing, call `connect` to link the new memory to related ones. Links make later recall better.
- To fix a memory, call `update_memory`. Do not store a second, corrected copy.
- Call `save_context` at milestones and before a handoff. Refer to key memories in the description as `memory_id: <uuid>`.
- Use artifacts for code and long documents. Because artifacts are not searched, also store a short memory with a description of the file and its exact path.
- Importance does not change search ranking. It is used for filtering and sorting.
- Content longer than 10,000 characters does not fit in one memory. Split it, store it as an artifact with a pointer memory, or have the user upload it as a document.

- [Penfield documentation home](https://docs.penfield.app/): what Penfield is and the five setup steps, from creating an account and configuring the AI personality to connecting an AI
- [Install Prompt](https://docs.penfield.app/install-prompt/): a prompt a user pastes into an AI so the AI can work out how to connect
- [Quick Reference](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/penfield-user-quick-reference/): how people use Penfield day to day, with example phrases
- [Example Custom Instructions](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/example-custom-instructions/): a starter template for personalizing an assistant

## Setup guides by platform

- [Antigravity](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/antigravity-setup/): add Penfield as a remote MCP server in Google Antigravity (app, IDE and CLI)
- [ChatGPT](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/chatgpt-setup/): add Penfield as a custom MCP plugin in ChatGPT
- [Claude](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/claude-setup/): add Penfield as a custom connector in Claude
- [Claude Code](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/claude-code-setup/): connect Claude Code in the terminal
- [Grok](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/grok-setup/): add Penfield as a custom connector in Grok
- [Manus](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/manus-setup/): connect Manus
- [MCP Remote](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/mcp-remote-setup/): Cursor, Windsurf, LM Studio and other apps that connect through mcp-remote
- [Perplexity](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/perplexity-setup/): connect Perplexity and the Comet browser
- [Other MCP Clients](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/other-clients/): connection details and generic steps for any MCP client
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.penfield.app/onboarding/reconnect-penfield/): check, reconnect and reinstall the connection

- [MCP Tool Reference](https://docs.penfield.app/mcp/mcp-integration/): every tool with its parameters, responses and error codes, and the mapping to REST endpoints

## REST API

- [API Overview](https://docs.penfield.app/api/): base URL, concepts, authentication summary, rate limit headers, error format
- [Quick Start](https://docs.penfield.app/api/guides/quick-start/): first token, first memory, first search, first relationship
- [Authentication](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/authentication/): API key exchange, device code flow, authorization code with PKCE, refresh tokens, scopes, discovery
- [Memories](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/memories/): create, get, list, update and delete memories
- [Search](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/search/): hybrid search, vector search, search stats
- [Relationships](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/relationships/): create, list, update, delete, bulk create and graph traversal
- [Documents](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/documents/): upload, chunking, list, download, delete
- [Artifacts](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/artifacts/): file storage, path rules, and how to make artifacts findable
- [Analysis](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/analysis/): reflect, summarize, insights, memory history, contradictions, evolve
- [Tags](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/tags/): add, remove and list tags, memories by tag, tag limits
- [Personality](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/personality/): personas and custom instruction traits
- [Awakening](https://docs.penfield.app/api/endpoints/awakening/): the briefing an AI loads at the start of a session
